name: cuda-api-wrappers
listed_description: Lightweight, Modern-C++ wrappers for the CUDA GPU programming runtime API.
reason: No numeric comparison anywhere reachable. README says the wrappers are thin and that their overhead 'vanishes almost entirely on compilation' (directional claim, no numbers, no named baseline); repo root has no benchmark directory (folders: .github, cmake, docs, examples, src/cuda; examples are modified CUDA samples and per-module usage). Issue #279 is about removing runtime-API use, with no timings; an issue search for overhead, benchmark and performance found no wrapper-versus-raw-CUDA timings. A web search found no third-party benchmark of the library. BSD-3-Clause, 906 stars, default branch master.

name: cupla
listed_description: C++ API to run CUDA/C++ on OpenMP, Threads, TBB, ... through Alpaka.
reason: No numeric comparison in the project. The listed URL is a stub README (1 commit) pointing to the moved repo https://github.com/alpaka-group/cupla (LGPL-3.0-or-later, 39 stars, default branch dev). That README and doc/TuningGuide.md, doc/PortingGuide.md and CHANGELOG.md say only that a find-and-replace CUDA port runs 'rather bad' on x86 and that, with a compile-time element count N=1, CUDA code 'will just stay with the very same performance' (qualitative, no numbers). Search snippets show alpaka (the backend, a separate project) reporting near-zero overhead against native CUDA and OpenMP in its 2016 paper (arXiv 1602.08477) and a DGEMM result, but arXiv is blocked here and those numbers are for alpaka, not cupla.

name: Cxxomfort
listed_description: A small, header-only library that backports various facilities from more recent C++ Standards to C++03 and later.
reason: No numeric comparison reachable. The project host ryan.gulix.cl does not resolve from this environment (getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND), so the fossil repository could not be opened. A web search found only the OSDN/Freshmeat project description (header-only C++11 backports for C++03, aimed at easing backward compatibility), with no performance claim; a feature-backport library has no natural speed baseline.

name: ffead-cpp
reason: Rank claim only, no numbers reachable. README says 'According to the latest tfb results, ffead-cpp [embedded+v-picov] is currently the 20th fastest web/http/sql framework in the world' and links to tfb-status.techempower.com, which does not resolve here (getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND). The TechEmpower FrameworkBenchmarks repo holds ffead-cpp configs and many dockerfiles (frameworks/C++/ffead-cpp), but no results; two web searches found no requests-per-second figure for ffead-cpp. README has no other benchmark section; root has siege.sh and .siegerc with no results. A rank is not a number against a named baseline. A retry from an environment that can reach TechEmpower results could yield a tier A or B web-server record. 748 stars; no LICENSE file in the root listing, so the licence is unclear.

name: FiberTaskingLib
listed_description: Task-based multi-threading library that supports task graphs with arbitrary dependencies.
reason: No numeric comparison reachable. README.asciidoc compares fibers with Intel TBB only qualitatively (a contrived dependency-chain scenario, no numbers). The benchmarks/ directory holds two Catch2 benchmarks (empty.cpp: 65000 empty tasks; producer_consumer.cpp) that time FiberTaskingLib alone, with no baseline library; issues #10, #142 and #145 concern its own benchmark tooling. A web search found no third-party benchmark including it, and the tzcnt/runtime-benchmarks README does not mention it. Apache-2.0, 987 stars, default branch master.

name: FTXUI
reason: No numeric comparison against an external baseline. README mentions 'performance tests' only as a good practice and names no baseline; CHANGELOG.md has speedups only against earlier FTXUI versions (for example Basic rendering about 27% faster, Styled rendering about 38% faster, Color building about 70x faster on non-truecolor terminals). A web search found no benchmark against ncurses, termbox, notcurses or Ratatui. MIT, 10.8k stars. The guessed category logging-tracing was wrong (it is a terminal UI library).
